title: World Anatomy Day 2026: Anatomy for All
location: College of Medicine, Gulf Medical University, Ajman
role: Organizing team member: event banner design, photography and timing the plank competition
description:
Gulf Medical University's College of Medicine marked World Anatomy Day on its campus in Ajman on 15 October 2026. The day was dedicated to Andreas Vesalius, the father of modern anatomy, and the year 2026 had the theme of “Anatomy for All”.

As part of a team of eight, I helped organize the event, which welcomed visiting high school students. Our main activity was a plank competition. High school students held a plank for as long as they could, and the student who held it the longest won. As they played, my team members explained the muscles involved in holding the plank to the students using an abdominal model.

I designed the event banner, took photographs of the competition, and timed the participants. The plank competition demonstrated creativity, by turning an anatomy concept into a fun interactive game that students could understand and enjoy. This was also my first experience coordinating an event at the university and with high school students.
takeaway: Anatomy becomes unforgettable the moment you make it something people can feel.

gibbs.description: On 15 October 2026, my team of eight and I organised World Anatomy Day at Gulf Medical University’s College of Medicine. We welcomed numerous high school students to come in and learn about the human body in a fun and interactive manner. To engage students, we held a plank competition in which the participant who held the position the longest won a prize. My teammates used an abdominal muscle model to show which muscles are used to maintain the position. I designed the event banner, took photographs of the competition, and timed the participants.
gibbs.feelings: I was nervous beforehand, as it was my first time organising an event at the university, and because I had to talk and interact with high school students. However, once the students began arriving and joining in, I felt more at ease and started to genuinely enjoy the experience. I also felt proud of the banner I had designed, especially when people complimented it.
gibbs.evaluation: The event overall was largely successful. We were able to actively involve the students, teach them, and answer their questions, with many of them participating in the plank competition. It was fun for all of us to watch and cheer on the participants. However, we did not assign roles clearly beforehand, which meant everyone ended up jumping in on every task. Moreover, we planned the event at the last minute, during the same week as midterms, so we had very little time to prepare.
gibbs.analysis: The plank competition successfully made learning a game. Students played against peers, and they had lots of fun, learning how the muscles assist them to maintain their position. This approach to learning is more active and participative than passively receiving explanations and is therefore more captivating and memorable. The muscle model provided students with a clear visual representation of the muscles activated and engaged while performing the plank position. Looking back, the lack of defined roles caused tasks to overlap, which showed me that clear responsibilities are essential for efficiency and accountability. Despite this, the team collaborated effectively and supported each other.
gibbs.conclusion: Through this experience, I learned that teamwork is most effective when there is structure, and that planning with defined roles can make a significant difference in how smoothly an event runs. I also realised I can handle unfamiliar situations, such as organising an event, and engage with high school students more confidently than I expected. Taking initiative and contributing wherever I was needed helped me grow as a collaborator, while turning an anatomy concept into a competition showed me that innovation in medical education can be simple, engaging and still effective.
gibbs.action_plan: In future events, I will ensure that roles and responsibilities are clearly divided and allocated at the initial planning stage so that every team member knows their exact duties beforehand. I will also start preparing well in advance, considering our academic and exam schedule early to avoid any last-minute pressure.
